shell.backend-down-body: This can happen the first time you open the app after installing or updating.
shell.backend-down-dev: Start the local services (scripts/dev.sh or scripts/dev.ps1), then reload.
shell.mode-browser-tooltip: Running in a browser dev session. Commands fall back to HTTP against the orchestrator (port 5100).
shell.theme-system: Theme: follow the system (click to switch)
shell.backend-restarting: at {{time}} (code {{code}}). VideoDubber is starting it again by itself; dubs that were running continue where they were.
shell.backend-failed-body: It stopped several times in a few minutes, so it is not started again. Restart the app; if it happens again, open Help and export a support bundle.
shell.backend-failed-start: VideoDubber's background service could not be started. Reinstall VideoDubber; Help has the details.
shell.backend-not-responding: The background service is running but not answering; it may be busy with a heavy step. Wait a minute; if it stays like this, restart the app.

update.installing-body: VideoDubber is downloading this in the background and will restart when it's ready.
update.no-notes: No release notes were published for this version.
update.install-failed: The update could not be installed. You can retry from Settings → Updates.
update.auto-waiting-body: It installs in the background the next time VideoDubber opens with no dub running, or you can install it now.

progress.keep-working: When the download is done, VideoDubber closes, installs the update and opens again by itself, in about a minute.
progress.installing: VideoDubber will close, install the update and open again by itself.
progress.ready: Installing closes VideoDubber for about a minute, so the update waits while a dub is running. Install it when your dub is done.
progress.busy: Installing an update closes VideoDubber, which would stop the dub. Install the update when the dub has finished, or pause the dub first.
progress.failed-title: The update could not be completed.
progress.failed-hint: Check the internet connection and try again. If it keeps failing, download the installer from GitHub and run it: your projects and settings stay as they are.

outcome.failed-title: The update to {{ to }} did not finish.
outcome.failed-body: VideoDubber is still version {{ from }}. Try again, or download the installer from GitHub: your projects and settings stay as they are.

ffmpeg-not-found.title: The video tool FFmpeg is missing
ffmpeg-not-found.fix: VideoDubber reads and writes video with FFmpeg, which comes with the app. Reinstall VideoDubber to bring it back.

ffprobe-not-found.title: The video tool ffprobe is missing
ffprobe-not-found.fix: VideoDubber reads a video's details with ffprobe, which comes with the app. Reinstall VideoDubber to bring it back.

ffmpeg-filter-missing.title: Subtitles cannot be burned into the picture
ffmpeg-filter-missing.fix: This copy of FFmpeg cannot draw subtitles on the video. Choose another subtitle option (a separate .srt or .vtt file, or soft subtitles inside the video), or reinstall VideoDubber.

python-not-found.title: A part of VideoDubber is missing (Python)
python-not-found.fix: Speech recognition, translation and voices run on the Python that comes with the app. Reinstall VideoDubber; if it happens again, export a support bundle from Help.

stt-model-missing.title: The speech recognition model is not downloaded
stt-model-missing.fix: Download a model in Settings → Speech-to-text, then try again.

translation-package-missing.title: The translation pack for these languages is not installed
translation-package-missing.fix: Install the pack for this language pair in Settings → Translation, or choose another translation engine.

piper-missing.title: The Piper voices are not set up
piper-missing.fix: Install a Piper voice in Voices, or choose another voice engine for this project.

tts-voice-missing.title: The chosen voice is not installed
tts-voice-missing.fix: Install it in Voices, or choose another voice.

unsupported-media.title: This video format is not supported
unsupported-media.fix: Use a common format such as MP4 (H.264 video with AAC sound), or convert the file with a video converter first.

no-audio-stream.title: This video has no sound
no-audio-stream.fix: There is no audio track to take the speech from. Choose a video with speech in it.

invalid-language.title: Unknown language
invalid-language.fix: Choose the language again from the list.

invalid-video-link.title: This link is not a video VideoDubber can download
invalid-video-link.fix: Paste the full address from your browser's address bar, for example a Bilibili or Douyin video page.

source-rate-limited.title: The video site is limiting downloads for now
source-rate-limited.fix: Wait a few minutes and try again. Finished downloads are kept, and an interrupted one continues where it stopped.

source-login-required.title: This video needs a signed-in account
source-login-required.fix: It is for members only, paid or age-restricted. Sign in to the site in your browser, then add its cookie on the Download screen.

source-unavailable.title: The site does not offer this video
source-unavailable.fix: It was removed, is private, or cannot be watched in your region. Open the link in a browser to check that it plays there.

disk-full.title: The disk is full
disk-full.fix: Free some space (Settings → Storage can clear finished downloads and caches), or move the projects folder to a larger drive, then try again.

output-not-writable.title: VideoDubber cannot save in this folder
output-not-writable.fix: Check that the folder still exists and that you may write in it (not a system folder or a disconnected drive), or choose another folder.

worker-unavailable.title: VideoDubber's background service is not answering
worker-unavailable.fix: It may still be starting, or restarting after a problem. Wait a moment and try again; if it keeps happening, quit and reopen VideoDubber.

worker-timeout.title: This took longer than its time limit
worker-timeout.fix: Try again: work already finished is kept. If it keeps happening, the troubleshooting guide (under Technical details) says what to change for each step.

cloud-credentials-missing.title: An API key is missing
cloud-credentials-missing.fix: This step uses an online service, but no key is saved for it. Add the key in Settings → Cloud services & keys, or switch the step back to an engine on this computer.

cloud-request-failed.title: The online service refused the request
cloud-request-failed.fix: Check that the API key is valid and has quota left, then try again; or switch the step to an engine on this computer.

engine-pack-missing.title: An engine this step needs is not installed
engine-pack-missing.fix: Install it in Settings → Engines & models, or choose another engine for this step.

engine-pack-failed.title: The engine could not be downloaded or checked
engine-pack-failed.fix: Check your internet connection and free disk space, then install it again. A damaged download is thrown away by itself.

engine-unavailable.title: An engine did not start
engine-unavailable.fix: Try the step again. If it keeps happening, reinstall the engine in Settings → Engines & models, or choose one that runs on the processor.

engine-busy.title: This engine is busy with another dub
engine-busy.fix: These engines take most of the computer and serve one project at a time. Wait for that dub to finish (or pause it), then try again.

cancelled.title: Stopped before it finished
cancelled.fix: Nothing finished so far is lost. Start it again when you are ready.

run-in-progress.title: Something is still running
run-in-progress.fix: Wait for it to finish, or pause it, then try again. Technical details say what is running.

invalid-edit.title: That edit cannot be applied
invalid-edit.fix: A line must start before it ends, stay inside the video and keep its place between its neighbours. Undo the last change or adjust it, then try again.

voice-consent-required.title: Your confirmation is needed to save this voice
voice-consent-required.fix: A cloned voice is saved only with your statement that it is your own voice or that its owner allowed it. Tick the statement in the dialog, then save again.

voice-reference-rejected.title: This recording cannot make a voice
voice-reference-rejected.fix: It needs at least 3 seconds of one person speaking clearly. Record again closer to the microphone, or pick another part of the file.

voice-engine-cannot-clone.title: This voice engine cannot speak cloned voices
voice-engine-cannot-clone.fix: It only has its own preset voices. Use VieNeu-TTS 3.8, which speaks cloned voices, or pick a preset voice for these lines.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, open Help and copy the diagnostics to report it.

source-video.title: Download a source video
source-video.subtitle: Fetch a video from Bilibili or Douyin to use as the source for a dubbing project.
source-video.link-label: Bilibili or Douyin links, one per line
source-video.link-hint: A full link, a short link (b23.tv, v.douyin.com), or just the video id all work. Paste several to download them one after another. A collection, favourites or an uploader's page link adds its videos (Check link lets you pick).
source-video.respect-notice: Only download videos you have the right to use, and please respect the people who made them.
source-video.quality-note: The best quality varies by video (usually 720p when signed out). Sign in below (optional) to download sharper videos.

session.heading: Sign in to download sharper videos (optional)
session.intro: Signed out, Bilibili gives at most 720p. If you have a Bilibili account, VideoDubber can use the sign-in of your browser to download up to 1080p (1080p+ and 4K also need a VIP account). It never sees your password.
session.step-sign-in: Open bilibili.com in your browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox) and sign in to your account.
session.step-extension: Add a browser extension that saves cookies to a file, such as “Get cookies.txt LOCALLY”. Pick one that works only on your computer and sends nothing anywhere.
session.step-export: With the bilibili.com tab open, click the extension and export the cookies of this site. It saves a file, usually named like bilibili.com_cookies.txt.
session.step-choose: Press “Choose the cookie file” below and pick that file. VideoDubber keeps only the two Bilibili cookies it needs and checks right away that the sign-in works.
session.step-delete: Then delete the cookie file: anyone who has it can use your account.
session.file-not-cookies: This is not a cookie file. Export the cookies again with the extension and choose the file it saves (it usually ends in .txt).
session.file-no-site: This file has no Bilibili cookies. Export the cookies while the bilibili.com tab is open, not another site.
session.file-signed-out: This file holds no Bilibili sign-in: you were signed out when it was saved. Sign in on bilibili.com, then export the cookies again.
session.file-too-big: This file is too big to be a cookie file. Choose the file the extension saved for bilibili.com.
session.paste-heading: Another way: paste the cookie yourself
session.paste-help: If you know your way around the browser's developer tools: paste the value of bilibili.com's SESSDATA cookie (or the whole Cookie header). Only SESSDATA and buvid3 are kept.
session.warning: Good to know: a sign-in works like a key to your account, so anyone who has it can use the account. VideoDubber keeps it only on this computer, in your own user folder, and sends it only to Bilibili. Remove it here at any time, or sign out on bilibili.com to make it stop working.
session.placeholder: Paste SESSDATA=… or just the value
session.valid: ✓ Signed in as {{name}}: downloads can be up to 1080p.
session.invalid: ✗ This sign-in no longer works (it expired, or you signed out on the site), so downloads stay at the lower quality. Sign in on bilibili.com again and choose a new cookie file.
session.mother-claude: Using Mother Claude? It can give VideoDubber your browser's Bilibili cookies by itself; the values never pass through the conversation.

source-video.quality-resolved-lower: This video does not offer that — will download at {{quality}}, the closest available.
source-video.all-parts: All parts of a multi-part video
source-video.all-parts-hint: A Bilibili video in several parts (P1, P2…) is added part by part.
source-video.queue-intro: Two download at a time; the others wait their turn. A download that did not finish (the app was closed, the connection dropped) continues where it stopped.
source-video.search-ph: Search by title, uploader, link or file…
source-video.no-match: No download matches this search or filter.
source-video.site-subtitles-title: The site's own subtitles were saved with the video: a project can use them as its transcript.
source-video.open-source-title: Open the video's page in your browser: {{url}}
source-video.retry-at: The site is limiting downloads for now; trying again at {{time}}.
source-video.remove-confirm-body: The file is deleted and the download leaves the list. Projects made from it keep their own copy.
source-video.dub-intro: Make a project for each ticked video with one of your presets. Save a preset in New project (Save as preset).
source-video.dub-no-presets: No presets yet: in New project, fill in the form and press Save as preset.
source-video.dub-split: Dub long videos as a series of parts
source-video.dub-split-hint: Only videos longer than {{min}} minutes are split; the others are dubbed whole. The AI picks the cuts among the pauses between lines and names each part; the parts are then made and dubbed one after another. To check the cuts first, dub that video from New project instead.
source-video.dub-split-no-ai: Long videos can be dubbed as a series of parts once an AI is set up in Settings: Claude (an API key, or your Claude plan through Mother Claude), OpenAI, Gemini, or the built-in Gemma chat model.
source-video.dub-done-split: {{n}} projects made; {{s}} long videos will be dubbed in parts.
source-video.dub-none: No project was made: the reason is under each video.
source-video.dub-queued: Waiting its turn: another dub is running.
source-video.dub-waiting: Starts by itself once the models it needs are downloaded.
source-video.dub-created: Project made, not started yet: start it on its page.
source-video.dub-series: Will be dubbed in parts, one after another.
source-video.list-count: {{n}} videos shown (the list has {{total}}). Untick the ones you do not want.
source-video.held-gpu-heavy: Paused while a dub is in a heavy step (dubbing comes first); it continues from where it stopped.
source-video.held-dubbing: Waiting until the dub finishes: on this computer one task runs at a time (Settings → Downloads).
source-video.held-pressure: Paused while the computer is short of memory; it continues by itself.

error.rate-limited: The site is limiting downloads from this computer for now.
error.rate-limited-fix: Wait a few minutes, then press Retry. Finished downloads are kept, and this one continues where it stopped.
error.login-required: This video can only be watched with a signed-in account (members only, paid, or age-restricted).
error.login-required-fix: Sign in to the site in your browser, let VideoDubber use that sign-in (above the list, under “Sign in to download sharper videos”), then press Retry.
error.unavailable: The site does not offer this video: it was removed, is private, or is not available in your country.
error.unavailable-fix: Open the link in your browser to check that the video plays there.
error.invalid-link: This link is not a video VideoDubber can download.
error.invalid-link-fix: Copy the full address of the video page from your browser's address bar (Bilibili or Douyin) and paste it again.

settings.title: Settings

language.label: Display language
language.hint: Applies to the whole app immediately, and is remembered next time you open it.

computer.heading: This computer
computer.cloud-suggest: For this machine, cloud processing is suggested for {{ phases }}: add an API key, then choose the cloud engine on that step's page.

defaults.render-value: Local FFmpeg — always on this machine (your video never leaves it).
defaults.unavailable: Couldn't load the engines to choose from: VideoDubber's background service isn't answering. If this lasts, restart the app.

claude.heading: Claude (AI assistant)
claude.intro: Let Claude run VideoDubber for you: create projects from a file or a link, dub them, read the whole transcript and rewrite the translation with full context, re-voice lines and render. Claude Desktop and Claude Code connect through MCP.
claude.privacy: Dubbing still runs on this computer. When you ask Claude to work on a project, the transcript and translations it reads are sent to Claude as part of your conversation.
claude.restart: Done. Quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again to load VideoDubber.
claude.try: Then ask Claude, for example: "Dub the video in my Downloads folder into Vietnamese with the best quality."
claude.no-server: This copy of VideoDubber is missing the part that Claude connects to, so Claude can't be connected. Quit and reopen VideoDubber; if this message is still here, reinstall the app.
claude.unavailable: Couldn't check whether Claude is connected: VideoDubber's background service isn't answering. If this lasts, restart the app.

code.other-copy: Points to another copy of VideoDubber
code.other-copy-hint: Claude Code starts VideoDubber from {{ path }}, not this app (after a reinstall or a move, for example). Reconnect points it here.
code.cli-missing-hint: Claude Code isn't installed on this computer, or VideoDubber can't find it. Install it, then come back here. If it is installed, you can run this command in a terminal instead:
code.unreadable-hint: {{ detail }}. Reconnect asks Claude Code to set VideoDubber up again.
code.connected-hint: New Claude Code sessions have VideoDubber's tools, including sessions you start in Mother Claude. Restart sessions that were already open.
code.manual: Or run it yourself in a terminal

keys.intro: Optional. Keys are saved only on this computer, in a file only your user account can open (~/VideoDubber/credentials.json), and are sent only to the service they belong to. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose a cloud engine for a step.
keys.claude-model: Claude model for translation and review
keys.claude-model-hint: Opus gives the most natural, consistent translation; Sonnet costs about half as much; Haiku is the cheapest and fastest. Roughly, a 30-minute video costs a few cents with Haiku and one to two US dollars with Opus.

mc.option-key-hint: Anthropic bills you per use. Create a key at console.anthropic.com and paste it below.
mc.option-mc: My Claude plan, through Mother Claude
mc.option-mc-hint: No API key: Claude Code on this computer answers through Mother Claude, signed in with your Claude account, so translation counts against your plan's usage limits.
mc.status-up: Mother Claude's HTTP API is running at {{ url }}.
mc.status-down: Mother Claude's HTTP API is not running at {{ url }}. Follow the steps below.
mc.status-key: Mother Claude answered, but its HTTP API has a key: paste that key below.
mc.check-failed: Couldn't check Mother Claude: VideoDubber's background service didn't answer. Try again in a moment.
mc.step-install: Install Mother Claude and open it. It uses the Claude account Claude Code is signed in with.
mc.step-open: In Mother Claude, open HTTP API. Under Access, set Reachable from to This computer.
mc.step-start: Press Start the API. Tick “Start when Mother Claude opens” so it is ready every time.
mc.step-test: Come back here and press Test: VideoDubber sends Claude one short message.
mc.url-hint: It is shown under Claude API on Mother Claude's HTTP API page. Change it only if you changed Mother Claude's port.
mc.key-placeholder: Empty: Mother Claude's HTTP API has no key
mc.key-saved: A key is saved — type a new one to replace it
mc.key-hint: Only if you set a key on Mother Claude's HTTP API: paste the same key here. Mother Claude shows a saved key only in part, so if you no longer have it, set a new one there and paste it here too.
mc.testing: Sending Claude a short message… The first one can take up to a minute while Mother Claude starts Claude Code.
mc.test-ok: Claude answered through Mother Claude ({{ model }}). You can translate with Claude now.
mc.key-kept: Your Anthropic API key ({{ masked }}) stays saved: choose “Anthropic API key” above to use it again.
mc.privacy: As with any cloud provider, the transcript goes to Claude (Anthropic) to be translated; the video and audio stay on this computer. Mother Claude keeps these conversations in its own data folder.
mc.model-hint: Through Mother Claude there is no per-use bill: translation counts against your Claude plan's usage limits, and Opus uses them up fastest.

engines.none: None of these engines are offered for this computer's operating system.
engines.load-failed-hint: VideoDubber's background service didn't send the list of engines, so this page can't show what is installed or what you can install. It may still be starting: try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, restart the app.

engines.fit-ok: ✓ Your hardware can run this locally

engines.use-this-title: Use this model instead of the automatic choice. A larger model translates better but runs slower when it does not fit the graphics card's memory.
engines.update-title: A newer version is available — reinstall to update
engines.reinstall-confirm-body: Reinstalling downloads all {{ size }} again and replaces the copy on this computer. It is only needed when this engine has stopped working. You can keep using the app while it downloads.
engines.needs-uv-title: This engine needs uv, which has no build for this platform

argos.intro: Offline Argos Translate language packs, downloaded from the Argos index on demand. Non-English pairs translate via English (e.g. Chinese → Vietnamese uses Chinese → English + English → Vietnamese), so install both legs for such a pair. Ollama / cloud translation are not limited to these.
argos.empty: Installed packs appear here. Click “Browse available packs” to see everything you can install.
argos.remove-failed: Couldn't remove the {{ from }} → {{ to }} pack. Try again; if it keeps failing, restart VideoDubber.

projects-folder.heading: Projects folder
projects-folder.intro: Where VideoDubber keeps your projects: each one in its own folder inside “projects”, with its working files and, unless you chose another folder for it, the finished video. Choosing another folder moves every project there, with the same structure.
projects-folder.example: {{ count }} projects. A finished video is saved like this:
projects-folder.unavailable: {{ folder }} cannot be reached (a drive that is not connected?). Connect it again, or go back to the default folder.
projects-folder.moving: Moving the projects to {{ folder }}… {{ done }} of {{ total }}
projects-folder.note: To move, every dub must be paused or finished. Engines, voice models and settings stay in VideoDubber’s own folder.
projects-folder.pick-title: Choose the folder for your projects
projects-folder.confirm-body: {{ count }} projects will move to {{ folder }}, each with all its files. Large videos can take a few minutes; until it has finished, projects cannot be changed.
projects-folder.unavailable-api: The projects folder cannot be shown: the background service is not running.

storage.heading: Storage
storage.intro: Downloaded engine packs, AI models, and caches all live in one app folder. Delete them anytime to free up disk space — VideoDubber re-downloads whatever a project needs on demand. Your projects (the dubbed videos) are never touched.
storage.unavailable: Storage info is unavailable (the background service may not be running).
storage.downloads-hint: Source videos from the Download screen. They are yours, so "Delete" above never touches them. Projects made from them keep their own copy.

updates.heading: Updates
updates.browser-note: Update controls are available in the desktop app. You're running in a browser dev session, so checking and installing updates is disabled here.
updates.auto-hint: When on, the app checks for updates on launch and installs them in the background. When off, you update manually below.

about.heading: About VideoDubber
about.body: A local, offline-first video dubbing app. Transcription, translation, and voice synthesis all run on your machine. Only the language models are downloaded on first run.

settings.brand-kit-intro: Your logos and spoken greetings, made once and chosen per project (New project, the editor, Export). A project keeps its own copy, so changing this list never changes a finished project.

downloads.intro: Downloading uses the network, the disk and the processor. This decides what downloads do while a dub runs; dubbing always comes first.
downloads.opt-pause-heavy: Download alongside, pausing during the dub's heavy steps
downloads.opt-one-task: One task at a time: downloads wait until the dub finishes
downloads.opt-no-limit: No limit: download alongside, two at a time
downloads.now-pause-heavy: Now: downloads run alongside dubs and pause during their heavy steps (a graphics card with 12 GB or more and room for two dubs counts as powerful). A paused download goes on from where it stopped.
downloads.now-one-task: Now: one task at a time. With less than 12 GB of graphics memory, or room for only one dub, a dub uses the whole computer, so downloads wait until it finishes and then go one at a time.
downloads.now-no-limit: Now: downloads run alongside dubs without pausing, two at a time. Dubs may be slower.
downloads.login-hint: Signing in to a site for better quality is on the Download screen (Source account).

dubbing.presets-empty: No presets yet. New projects start from the settings recommended for this computer.

fn.open-voices-hint: Listen to, install and favourite the voices of every engine, and make your own, on the Voices screen.

builtin.faster-whisper-hint: Comes with the app and runs on any computer. Its speech models download once, the first time a project needs them, or here.
builtin.phowhisper-hint: Whisper trained further on Vietnamese by VinAI: the most accurate choice for videos spoken in Vietnamese. Runs on the built-in faster-whisper.
builtin.models-unavailable: Could not tell which models are downloaded: is the background service running?
builtin.model-distil: Distil Large v3.5 — English only, fastest large (~760 MB)

whisper.title: Whisper
whisper.desc: OpenAI's speech recognition, run on this computer: it writes down what is said, with timings. Bigger models are more accurate and slower; the one recommended for this computer is marked.

translategemma.title: TranslateGemma
translategemma.desc: Google's open translation model, run on this computer: far better than Argos, and offline. It comes in three sizes and one runs at a time: the best this computer runs well, or the one you choose. 4B runs on any computer with 8 GB of RAM; 12B and 27B want a graphics card or Apple Silicon.

gemma-chat.title: Gemma (translation with context, and review)
gemma-chat.desc: Google's Gemma models follow instructions, so they translate whole scenes with the project's character sheet (names, terms, forms of address), review a finished translation, and shorten lines too long to speak in time. One runs at a time: the best this computer runs well, or the one you choose.

llama-cpp.title: llama.cpp (runs TranslateGemma and Gemma)
llama-cpp.desc: The program that runs the TranslateGemma and Gemma models on this computer. It installs by itself with the first model; when several builds are installed, the fastest one this computer can use runs.

libretranslate.title: LibreTranslate
libretranslate.desc: A LibreTranslate server on this computer. Its engine is Argos, so it translates exactly as the built-in Argos does, with your Argos language packs: install it only if you want the server itself.

vieneu.title: VieNeu (natural Vietnamese voices)
vieneu.desc: Vietnamese voices far more natural than Piper. VieNeu-TTS 3.8 is the newest: 25 voices across the three regions, and voice cloning. Neural TTS v3 keeps the ten voices of projects made before it. Each has a processor build and an NVIDIA build about 4× faster, which falls back to the processor when the card cannot be used.

zerotts.title: ZeroTTS
zerotts.desc: Eight natural Vietnamese voices (young, middle-aged and older; storytelling, news and commentary) on the processor: the most accurate Vietnamese reader measured.

kokoro.title: Kokoro
kokoro.desc: A small, fast voice model: 54 voices in English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian and Portuguese (no Vietnamese).

supertonic.title: Supertonic
supertonic.desc: Ten voices that each speak 31 languages, Vietnamese included, though they read it slowly: VieNeu or ZeroTTS fit Vietnamese timing better. Its maker has archived it, so no more updates.

omnivoice.title: OmniVoice
omnivoice.desc: A voice model for more than 600 languages, on Apple Silicon only.

speaker-detection.title: Speaker detection
speaker-detection.desc: Works out who says each line, so every person in the video can get their own voice and the translator knows who is talking to whom. Runs on the processor in about a tenth of the video's length; turn it on per project (“Detect who speaks”).

separation.title: Music & voice separation
separation.desc: Takes the voices apart from the music and sound effects, so “Replace voices, keep music & effects” keeps the soundtrack at full volume under the dub, and a voice copied from the video comes out clean. About a tenth of the video's length on a graphics card, about its length on the processor alone.

alignment.title: Forced alignment
alignment.desc: Word-accurate timings, for a tighter sync.

subtitle-reading.title: Reading burned-in subtitles
subtitle-reading.desc: Reads the subtitles drawn into a video's picture as text, on the processor (RapidOCR), so a video's own subtitles can be its transcript instead of speech-to-text: turn it on per project (“Use the subtitles burned into the picture”). Chinese and English subtitles, a few minutes per hour of video.

engine-notes.whisper-cpp: Runs Whisper on the NVIDIA graphics card, several times faster than the processor. It needs the model of the size each project uses: install the sizes you use below.
engine-notes.vieneu-tts: 25 natural voices across the North, Centre and South, and voice cloning from a short recording. The one to choose for new projects.
engine-notes.neural-tts: The ten voices of the earlier VieNeu, which projects made with them keep using.
engine-notes.audio-cpp: The program that runs the separation model; it installs with the model. On Windows the processor build installs beside the graphics-card one, as its fallback.

provider-notes.llama-cpp: Translates line by line with TranslateGemma: accurate and fast, but it sees one line at a time, so a Gemma review is added when Gemma is installed.
provider-notes.llama-cpp-chat: Gemma translates whole scenes with the character sheet: the most consistent offline translation, and slower.
provider-notes.argos-llm-repair: Argos drafts quickly, then Gemma fixes names, pronouns and terms with the character sheet.
provider-notes.argos: Comes with the app: offline and quick, but word for word. It needs the language pack of each pair (below).
provider-notes.ollama: TranslateGemma in Ollama, a separate program you install and run yourself (ollama.com).
provider-notes.openai-stt: Sends the audio to OpenAI to be transcribed. Needs an OpenAI key.
provider-notes.openai-translate: Translates with OpenAI's models, with the whole video as context. Needs an OpenAI key.
provider-notes.anthropic-translate: Translates with Claude, with the whole video as context. Needs an Anthropic key, or your Claude plan through Mother Claude.
provider-notes.gemini-translate: Translates with Google Gemini, with the whole video as context. Needs a Gemini key.
provider-notes.piper-local: Comes with the app: quick voices in many languages, less natural than VieNeu or ZeroTTS. Pick and download its voices on the Voices screen.
provider-notes.openai-tts: OpenAI's cloud voices, in many languages. The text is sent to OpenAI; needs an OpenAI key.
