export.title: Export
export.load-failed-body: The app may still be starting, or the project was deleted. Try again in a moment.
export.preview-unavailable: This video can't be played inside VideoDubber. Play it in your video player instead; if it was moved or deleted, render it again below.
export.not-made-body: The finished video is made in the last step of the dub. Follow the dub, or start it, on its progress page.
export.rerender-intro: Make the finished video again with the subtitle choice below. Changes made since the last render are included: if the dub sound changed (edited lines, mix settings), it is mixed again first. It runs like a dub, so you can follow it, pause it, or let it wait in the queue, and it uses the render quality from the project's settings.
export.busy-running: This project is being dubbed right now, so it can't be rendered again yet. Pause the dub first: nothing done is lost, and you can continue it later.
export.busy-queued: This project is waiting in the dubbing queue, so it can't be rendered again yet. Take it out of the queue first, or wait until its dub is done.

output-folder.title: Save to
output-folder.default-place: This is the project's own folder inside VideoDubber's data (the default). You can choose any other folder.
output-folder.chosen-place: A folder you chose for this project.
output-folder.dialog-title: Choose where to save this project's finished video
output-folder.locked: The folder can be changed once this project stops processing.
output-folder.hint: Only the finished video and its subtitle files (.srt, .vtt) are saved here. VideoDubber's working files (audio, voice clips, drafts) stay in its own data folder. Each project can be saved to a different folder.
output-folder.more: How files are named and moved
output-folder.naming-hint: In a folder you choose, the files are named after the project and its language, for example “{{ example }}”, so several projects can share one folder without overwriting each other.
output-folder.moved-hint: If the video has already been made, changing the folder moves it (and its subtitle files) to the new folder.
output-folder.browser-hint: Type or paste the full path of a folder on this computer. In the desktop app, “Choose folder…” opens a folder picker instead.
output-folder.change-failed: VideoDubber couldn't change where this project is saved.
output-folder.change-failed-fix: Choose a folder you can write to (not a read-only or protected location) and give its full path. If the video is open in another app, such as a video player, close it and try again.

processing.title: Dubbing progress
processing.stream-offline-title: The live event stream is disconnected
processing.load-failed-body: The app may still be starting, or the project was deleted. Try again in a moment.
processing.ready-body: The dub is finished and saved. Watch it, find it in its folder, or polish any line in the editor.
processing.start-body: This dub hasn't started yet. Start it and VideoDubber transcribes, translates and voices the video: you can follow each step here, and pause at any time without losing anything.
processing.preflight-and-more: {{ message }} (and {{ more }} more problem(s) to fix first)
processing.queued-title: ⏳ Waiting to start — #{{ position }} in the queue
processing.queue-reason-no-slot: It starts by itself as soon as a running dub finishes.
processing.queue-reason-heavy-busy: This dub needs the computer to itself, so it starts as soon as the work using it now finishes.
processing.queue-reason-paused: The queue is paused, so no new dub starts until you resume it.
processing.queue-capacity: This computer dubs {{ max }} project(s) at a time.
processing.review-body: The transcript is transcribed and translated — no voice has been synthesized yet. Review and adjust the lines (text, per-line fixes, the cast & pronoun sheet), then continue dubbing.
processing.degraded: ⚠ {{ services }} currently unavailable. The run may stall on the affected step until the service is back — services start a few seconds after launch.
processing.pause-hint: Your progress is saved: you can close VideoDubber or turn off the computer, and continue later.
processing.paused-body: Everything done so far is saved, even if you close VideoDubber or turn off the computer. Continue dubbing picks up where it stopped: finished steps are not redone, and the step that was running keeps the part it had finished (translated lines, voice clips).
processing.warnings: What this dub did on its own
processing.queue-reason-pressure: The computer is short of memory while another dub runs, so this render waits for that dub to finish: run beside it, both would slow to a crawl.
processing.dismiss-warning-hint: Set this warning aside once you have checked it. It comes back if the step runs again and finds the same.
processing.held-title: ⚠️ {{count}} line(s) still fail the translation checks
processing.held-body: The dub stopped before making any voice, because "Stop before voicing while lines still fail the translation checks" is on. Fix the lines marked in the editor (Problems), then continue dubbing: it voices the lines as they are then.
processing.queue-reason-gpu-hold: {{ app }} is using the graphics card (a live session), so this dub starts when it is done. Nothing that is already running is stopped.

onboarding.title: Welcome to VideoDubber
onboarding.s1-body: VideoDubber turns a video's spoken audio into another language — transcribe, translate, synthesize a new voice, and remux — all on this machine, fully offline once set up.
onboarding.s1-before: Before your first project we'll quickly:
onboarding.s1-li1: Check this machine has everything it needs to run.
onboarding.s1-li2: Let you pick your source & target languages and a transcription model.
onboarding.s1-li3: Download the AI models for those languages. This needs an internet connection and can take several minutes depending on the model size.
onboarding.s1-hint: The app, media tools and services are already bundled — only the language models are fetched on first run.
onboarding.s2-warn: Some checks need attention — you can still continue, but downloads or dubbing may fail until they're resolved.
onboarding.s2-unavailable: Couldn't run the checks yet. Make sure the local services have started, then re-check.
onboarding.s3-same-lang: Source and target language must be different.
onboarding.s3-no-pair: No prebuilt translation package is listed for {{ from }} → {{ to }}. The app will try to fetch one, but it may not be available offline.
onboarding.s3-no-catalog: Model catalog unavailable. The default model will be used once services are reachable.
onboarding.s3-total: Total download for these choices: ≈ {{ size }} MB.
onboarding.s3-voice-download: Download a Piper voice for {{ lang }}
onboarding.s3-voice-hint: A natural offline voice. You can pick a different voice (or add more) later from Settings.
onboarding.s3-no-voice: No bundled Piper voice is listed for {{ lang }} yet. You can add one later from Settings; dubbing will fall back to an available voice.
onboarding.s4-done: ✓ All set — your language models are installed.
onboarding.s4-fetching: Fetching the AI models for {{ from }} → {{ to }} — this one-time download needs an internet connection. Keep this window open.
onboarding.s4-retry-hint: Check your internet connection, then retry — it picks up the remaining models.
onboarding.s4-ready: You're ready to create your first project.
onboarding.s4-background: Keep this window open until the download finishes — closing it stops the download.
onboarding.skip: Skip for now — I'll download later
onboarding.skip-hint: Skipping is safe: when you create your first project, VideoDubber downloads exactly what that project needs before it starts.

check.media-tool-fix: A video tool that comes with VideoDubber is missing. Reinstall VideoDubber to bring it back.
check.service-fix: This background service did not start. Close VideoDubber and open it again; if it still fails, Help has a self-check and a report you can send.
check.network-fix: VideoDubber could not reach the site the models download from. You can continue, but the download needs an internet connection.
check.disk-fix: There may not be enough room for the models. Free up a few GB (5 GB or more is comfortable) before downloading the larger models.

editor.title: Editor
editor.preview-unavailable: In-app preview is unavailable here (the browser cannot load local files directly). Use “Open output folder” to play the video.
editor.settings-intro: Review every option applied to this dub. Change an engine, model or voice below, then re-dub from the affected stage — the earlier stages are reused (e.g. a new voice re-renders without redoing transcription or translation).
editor.refine-hint: Review & refine re-reads the whole transcript with a context-capable AI and polishes pronouns/terminology (re-dub from “Review & refine” to apply). Model size (e.g. TranslateGemma 4B → 12B) is managed in Settings → Engines.
editor.voice-from-video-hint: Makes the dub sound like the person in the video: the app clones their voice from the video's own audio (VieNeu-TTS 3.8, on this computer). Best for a video with one speaker. With several speakers, select one person's lines on the timeline and use “Make a voice from these lines” in the Line tab.
editor.speakers-hint: Give each person in the video their own voice. Every line of a speaker is spoken in that speaker's voice, unless the line has a voice of its own. Changing a voice marks the lines it affects for re-voicing.
editor.speakers-none: No speakers yet. Use “Detect speakers” above (it needs the Speaker detection engine, Settings → Engines), or set who says a line in the Line tab (select several lines to set them at once).
editor.subtitle-position-hint: Automatic puts the dub's subtitles just above the video's own burned-in subtitles when the app has found them (see "Picture" below) and they are not covered; otherwise at the bottom. Bottom always draws at the bottom.
editor.cover-original-hint: Many videos have their own subtitles burned in. Under "Picture" below, the app finds where they are, and you choose to blur them or cover them with a solid band.
editor.redub-title: Run the dub again from “{{ step }}”: this step and every step after it are done again; the steps before it are kept.
editor.redub-title-retranslate: Run the dub again from “{{ step }}”: every line is translated again, which also replaces the translations you edited or locked. The steps before it are kept.
editor.redub-locked-body: {{ n }} line(s) have a translation you wrote or locked by hand. Re-dubbing from “{{ step }}” translates every line again, so these are replaced with new machine translations too.
editor.redub-recommended: Your changes take effect from {{ step }} — click that stage to re-dub.
editor.redub-none: No changes yet. You can still re-dub from any stage (e.g. after installing a different model in Settings → Engines).
editor.ctx-intro: Used by context-aware translation (cloud LLMs, Gemma 3 chat, Argos + Gemma repair) to keep pronouns, terms of address, and terminology consistent. Fix something once — e.g. “student → teacher: gọi ‘thầy’, xưng ‘em’” — then Save & re-translate to apply it everywhere.
editor.ctx-ignored: The translation engine this project uses (Argos) translates one sentence at a time and cannot read any of this. Switch to an AI translation engine above to make the character sheet take effect.
editor.synopsis-ph: What is this video about, and who is talking to whom?
editor.pronouns-ph: Per speaker pair, the address terms to use (e.g. học sinh → giáo viên: gọi 'thầy', xưng 'em').
editor.save-retranslate-title: Save the sheet, then translate every line again with it. This also replaces the translations you edited or locked.
editor.no-sheet: No translation character sheet yet — one is generated automatically on the first context-aware translation run (cloud LLM, Gemma 3 chat, or Argos + Gemma repair), or create one now to steer pronouns and terminology.
editor.sheet-failed: The app tried to build the character sheet with "{{ engine }}" and could not ({{ why }}). Without it, names and forms of address can change from line to line. Write the sheet here, or pick a stronger review model, then re-translate.
editor.review-hint: No voice has been made yet. Check the lines (your edits save by themselves) and, in the Project tab, the cast & translation context, then press Continue dubbing to go on to making the voices.
editor.no-segments: No lines yet. Run the dub through the transcription and translation steps first.
editor.untranslated-title: The translation is identical to the source — the translator likely skipped this line. Edit it or re-run translation.

quality.wrong-script-title: The line still contains characters of another script (Chinese, Thai…), which the voice cannot read. Edit the line.
quality.pinyin-title: A word looks like romanized Chinese (pinyin) rather than the target language — often a name left untranslated. Edit the line.
quality.alternatives-title: The line offers alternatives with a slash (e.g. "thầy/cô"); the voice would read both. Pick one.
quality.no-diacritics-title: Several words with no Vietnamese diacritics — probably not Vietnamese. Edit the line.

editor.tighten-title: Shorten this line's translation so it fits its time window, keeping its meaning, then re-voice it
editor.diarize-hint: Works out who says each line when the dub is made again from speech-to-text. Needs the Speaker detection engine (Settings → Engines, ~135 MB).
editor.speakers-detect-hint: Works out who says each line from the video's audio, in seconds, without transcribing again: your translations and timing stay. If you know how many people speak, choose the number — it is much more reliable. Lines whose voice changes are marked for re-voicing.
editor.speakers-detect-gone: Speaker detection stopped: VideoDubber's background service restarted while it was running. Try again; the parts already done are kept.
editor.speakers-detect-failed: Speaker detection did not finish. Try again; the parts already done are kept.
editor.speaker-merge-label: Merge Speaker {{ n }} into another speaker
editor.loop-suspect-title: Speech-to-text may have repeated a phrase here that was not said (a known Whisper fault over music). The app tried to repair it and could not: listen to the original and fix or remove the line.
editor.speaker-guess-title: Speaker detection gave this line only a best guess (music, voices at once, or no clear turn). Check who says it, and set the speaker if it is wrong.
editor.cast-hint: Gives every speaker a voice of their gender: your cloned voices first, then the built-in ones, the deeper voices to the deeper speakers. You see the choice before anything changes.
editor.cast-unconfirmed: {{n}} of your cloned voices were left out because their gender is not confirmed: {{names}}. Confirm them in Voices → My voices and choose again, or apply without them.
editor.cast-refused: Not applied: some of your cloned voices would be left out. Tick the box below to apply without them.
editor.cast-without-clones: Apply without the voices left out
editor.cast-minor-auto: Automatic (3–6, by how many there are)
editor.cast-minor-hint: The speakers past the voices of their own (minor parts: a guard, a passer-by) share a few voices of their gender, taken from the built-in voices no main speaker has — never one of your cloned voices unless you choose it. Speakers who answer each other get different voices. Automatic gives 3 to 6 voices, about ten speakers each; choose a number to change it. Saved with “Apply these voices”.
editor.cast-pool-male: {{ n }} minor male speakers share {{ k }} voices:
editor.cast-pool-female: {{ n }} minor female speakers share {{ k }} voices:
editor.cast-pool-shared: also the voice of Speaker {{ n }}
editor.cast-soundalike: The built-in voice “{{ voice }}” is not shared out: it sounds like your cloned voice “{{ clone }}”.
editor.cast-unknown-title: Gender unknown ({{ n }}): they keep the project voice until you choose theirs in the list below.

cast-note.print-male: Male voices were matched to the male speakers by how they sound.
cast-note.print-female: Female voices were matched to the female speakers by how they sound.
cast-note.order-male: Not every male speaker and voice has a measured pitch, so the men who speak most got the voices in list order.
cast-note.order-female: Not every female speaker and voice has a measured pitch, so the women who speak most got the voices in list order.
cast-note.none-male: No male voice to choose from: {{ n }} male speaker(s) keep the project voice.
cast-note.none-female: No female voice to choose from: {{ n }} female speaker(s) keep the project voice.
cast-note.pool-male: {{ n }} minor male speakers share {{ k }} voices, about {{ each }} each; speakers who answer each other get different voices where possible.
cast-note.pool-female: {{ n }} minor female speakers share {{ k }} voices, about {{ each }} each; speakers who answer each other get different voices where possible.
cast-note.reused-male: Not enough built-in male voices are left over, so the voices of the cast speakers who speak least (speakers {{ speakers }}) are shared too.
cast-note.reused-female: Not enough built-in female voices are left over, so the voices of the cast speakers who speak least (speakers {{ speakers }}) are shared too.
cast-note.no-pool-male: No built-in male voice is free for {{ n }} minor speaker(s): they keep the project voice. Choose voices for them.
cast-note.no-pool-female: No built-in female voice is free for {{ n }} minor speaker(s): they keep the project voice. Choose voices for them.
cast-note.soundalike: The built-in voice “{{ voice }}” is not shared out: it sounds like your cloned voice “{{ clone }}”.
cast-note.unknown: {{ n }} speaker(s) of unknown gender keep the project voice: pick their voice in the list below.

editor.held-title: ⚠️ {{count}} line(s) still fail the translation checks.
editor.held-hint: No voice has been made yet. Fix the lines marked under Problems (your edits save by themselves), then press Continue dubbing.
editor.flagged-title: ⚠️ {{count}} line(s) still fail the translation checks after two repairs.
editor.flagged-hint: They were voiced as they are. Fix each one, or keep it as it is when it is right.
editor.use-burned-in-hint: Each subtitle drawn into the picture becomes a line instead of transcribing the speech (Chinese and English subtitles; needs the subtitle reader from Settings → Engines & models). Takes effect when speech-to-text runs again (Re-dub from: Transcribe (STT)).

studio.toggle-lines: Show or hide the line list
studio.save-error: Not saved — see the message above
studio.voice-changed-title: Re-synthesize every line whose text, voice or speed changed since it was last voiced.
studio.render-title: Re-mix the dub from this timeline and render the final video. Transcription and translation are reused.
studio.render-stale-title: Some edits are not voiced yet
studio.render-stale-body: {{ n }} line(s) changed since they were last voiced. Their old audio would end up in the video. Voice them first, then render?
studio.render-why-no-voices-title: The dub stopped before its voices were made. Continue it on its progress page, then render here.
studio.continue-title: Save your edits and go on to making the voices.
studio.running-note: This video is being dubbed right now. You can edit it again once the dub has finished.
studio.read-only-hint: Editing is paused while this video is being dubbed.
studio.stop-dub-body: This video is being dubbed right now. Going ahead stops that dub first; what it has already finished is kept.
studio.drop-hint: Drag a voice chip onto a line or clip to give it that voice. Drop an .srt or .vtt file on the timeline to import its text by timing.
studio.key-in-out: Set start / end to the playhead
studio.key-nosnap: Hold while dragging to stop snapping
studio.video-unavailable: The video can't be played in the preview. Editing still works; render to check the result.
studio.monitor-mix-title: Hear it the way it will render: the dub over the original, ducked (or removed) as the project's mix settings say.
studio.show-source: Show the source line under the subtitle
studio.preview-no-audio: This system blocked audio playback for the preview.
studio.preview-clip-failed: Some dub clips could not be loaded for the preview. Re-voice those lines if they stay silent.
studio.snap-title: Snap to the playhead and to neighbouring lines while dragging (hold Alt to override)
studio.follow-title: Keep the playhead in view while playing
studio.import-done: Imported text for {{ n }} line(s) from {{ file }}.
studio.import-unsupported: Only .srt and .vtt subtitle files can be imported.
studio.reading-speed: Reads too fast or too long
studio.bulk-hint: Changes here apply to every selected line. Drag any of them on the timeline to move them together.
studio.start-to-playhead: Set the start to the playhead
studio.end-to-playhead: Set the end to the playhead
studio.cps-title: Reading speed. Above about {{ max }} characters per second, viewers struggle to finish a subtitle.
studio.stale-title: The text, voice or speed changed since this line was voiced; the clip on the timeline is the old take.
studio.tighten-kept: Line {{ n }} was kept as it was: {{ reason }}. Shorten it by hand, or let the voice speed up.
studio.locked-title: Locked lines are never rewritten by auto-fit or review-and-refine.
studio.regenerate-title: Synthesize this line again with its current text, voice and speed.
studio.nothing-selected-hint: Click a line in the list or on the timeline. Drag lines to fix their timing; the dub follows instantly.
studio.voice-from-line: This line uses its own voice: {{ label }}.
studio.voice-chips: Voices you can drag onto lines
studio.voice-drag-title: Drag onto a line or clip on the timeline
studio.speaker: Speaker
studio.speaker-hint: Who says this line. A speaker's lines share that speaker's voice (Project tab → Speakers). Speaker detection fills this in; correct it here when it is wrong.
studio.voice-from-this-line: Make a voice from this line…
studio.voice-from-lines: Make a voice from these {{ n }} lines…
studio.voice-from-lines-hint: Copies the voice of whoever speaks these lines in the video. Select lines of one person only: about 10 seconds of clear speech in total works best (3 seconds at least).
studio.voice-made-applied: The selected line(s) now use “{{ name }}”. Re-voice them to hear it.
studio.voice-made-engine: “{{ name }}” is ready. To use it, set the voice engine to VieNeu-TTS 3.8 in the Project tab, then pick the voice for these lines.
studio.no-voices: This voice engine has no selectable voices.
studio.rate-hint: Faster reading fits a long line without the time-stretch artefacts. Takes effect when the line is re-voiced.

tighten-why.shortest: it is already as short as it can be
tighten-why.no-model: no AI model is available to shorten it (choose a review model in the Project tab, or install the Gemma chat model in Settings → Engines)
tighten-why.nothing: the AI model gave back nothing usable
tighten-why.echo: the AI model only gave back the original line
tighten-why.neighbour: the shorter version copied a neighbouring line
tighten-why.not-shorter: the AI model's version was no shorter
tighten-why.cut-too-far: the shorter version cut away too much of the meaning
tighten-why.refused: the shorter version did not pass the checks
tighten-why.checks: the shorter version failed the line checks ({{ problems }})

fit-why.no-window: This line has no time of its own to be spoken in: make it longer on the timeline.
fit-why.sped-up: Sped up to {{ x }}× to fit its time.
fit-why.sped-up-over: Sped up to {{ x }}× and still {{ s }} s too long: it runs into the pause after it (up to {{ allowed }} s is allowed).
fit-why.over: {{ s }} s too long: it runs into the pause after it (up to {{ allowed }} s is allowed).
fit-why.into-next: Still {{ s }} s too long even sped up to {{ x }}×: it runs into the next line. Shorten the translation (Tighten to fit can do it).
fit-why.beyond: Still {{ s }} s too long even sped up to {{ x }}×, more than the {{ allowed }} s allowed. Shorten the translation (Tighten to fit can do it).
fit-why.native-rate: The voice reads it {{ x }}× faster on its own to fit, with no time-stretch.

studio.keep-as-is-title: This line is right as it is: lock it, so it no longer counts as flagged and no automatic pass rewrites it. Unlock it (or undo) to flag it again.
studio.kept-as-is-title: Kept as it is: this finding of the checks is set aside.

wizard.title: New project
wizard.keep-hint: Music and effects stay; the original audio is automatically turned down whenever the dubbed voice speaks.
wizard.replace-vocals-hint: Studio-style: the original voices are separated out and replaced by the dub, while the music & effects play at full volume. Separation takes about a tenth of the video's length on a graphics card or Apple Silicon, about the video's length on a processor alone.
wizard.remove-hint: Only the dubbed voice is heard. Original speech, music and effects are all muted.
wizard.duck-level: Background volume while the dub speaks
wizard.forced-alignment-hint: Tightens subtitle/dub sync to ~50 ms using the “Forced alignment + diarization” engine.
wizard.fa-not-installed: Not installed — falls back to the default timestamps (install the engine in Settings → Engines for word-accurate timing).
wizard.diarize-hint: Works out who says each line, so every person can get their own voice (Editor → Project → Speakers) and the translator knows who is talking to whom. Adds about a tenth of the video's length to the dub.
wizard.auto-fit: Auto-fit lines that overflow their timing
wizard.auto-fit-hint: When a translated line is too long to fit even at max speed, re-translate it shorter and re-synthesize so it fits — fewer timing conflicts. Works with LLM translators (Ollama / llama.cpp / cloud); ignored for Argos.
wizard.auto-hint: Uses this computer's hardware video encoder (NVIDIA, Intel, AMD or Apple) when it works — checked once per session — and the software encoder otherwise. In our tests it looked as good as the software encoder and was 4–5× faster. Only matters when subtitles are burned in.
wizard.quality-hint: Encodes on the processor: the smallest files, but several times slower. Only matters when subtitles are burned in.
wizard.fast-hint: Uses the GPU video encoder (VideoToolbox / NVENC) when available — much faster, slightly larger files.
wizard.max-speed-hint: Translated speech is often longer than the original line. The app may speed lines up to this limit to keep them in sync; lines that still don't fit are flagged for review in the editor.
wizard.engines-hint: Each phase can run locally (private, free, works offline) or in the cloud (often better quality on weaker hardware; needs an API key from Settings and sends that phase's data to the service). Defaults come from Settings → Engines & models.
wizard.refine-hint: A second AI pass re-reads the whole transcript and polishes pronouns, terminology, and flow for consistency. Most useful when Translation runs on Argos or TranslateGemma.
wizard.review-pause: Pause for transcript review before voice synthesis
wizard.review-pause-hint: The dub stops once the transcript is translated (and refined) so you can review and hand-adjust the lines in the editor, then continue dubbing when it reads right.
wizard.rendering-hint: Local FFmpeg — always on this machine; your video never leaves it.
wizard.cloud-warn: ☁ Cloud processing enabled for: {{ phases }}. Only that data is uploaded — the video file itself stays local.
wizard.engines-unavailable: Engine list unavailable (background service not running?) — the project will use the local engines.
wizard.voice-omni: Choose a designed voice for OmniVoice. OmniVoice is multilingual, so these work for {{ lang }} (and any language); they ship with the engine pack — if it isn't installed yet, you'll be prompted to install it when the dub starts.
wizard.voice-vieneu: Choose a VieNeu voice for {{ lang }}. These ship with the VieNeu engine pack — if it isn't installed yet, you'll be prompted to install it when the dub starts.
wizard.voice-piper: Choose the Piper voice for {{ lang }}. Any voice not yet on this machine is downloaded automatically when you select it.
wizard.voice-needs-download: This voice isn't installed yet — it downloads automatically when the dub starts (or pick it again to fetch it now).
wizard.voice-omni-fail: Couldn't load the OmniVoice voices — the local services may still be starting. They'll be available once the engine is ready.
wizard.voice-vieneu-vi-only: VieNeu currently provides Vietnamese voices only. For {{ lang }}, pick Piper or a cloud provider in “Processing engines” above.
wizard.voice-library: Choose a {{ engine }} voice for {{ lang }}. Its voices come with the engine; if it is not installed yet, you will be asked to install it when the dub starts.
wizard.voice-library-none: {{ engine }} has no voice for {{ lang }}. Pick another voice engine in “Processing engines” above, or browse the Voices screen.
wizard.voice-browse: Listen to and compare every voice on the Voices screen →
wizard.voice-listen-making: Making a sample with this voice… The first one can take a few seconds while the engine starts.
wizard.voice-no-sample: This voice has no sample yet. Install it on the Voices screen to hear it.
wizard.voice-piper-none: Piper has no prebuilt voice for {{ lang }} yet — dubbing will fall back to an available voice. To get a natural voice, switch Text to speech to a cloud provider in “Processing engines” above.
wizard.workspace-note: A workspace is created when you continue.
wizard.more-hint: Subtitles, logo & greeting, original audio, timing and speaker detection, splitting into parts, video quality, speech speed, processing engines and voice. The defaults suit most videos.
wizard.no-audio-warn: ⚠ This file has no audio stream — there is nothing to transcribe or dub. Pick a different source.
wizard.probe-failed: Media could not be probed automatically. You can still start — the dub checks the file as its first step.
wizard.preparing-hint: Downloading the AI models for your selected languages — Start unlocks once they're ready (this continues in the background).
wizard.prep-failed: Some of the models these languages need did not download.
wizard.prep-failed-hint: Check the internet connection and try again: what already downloaded is kept. Or go back and choose other languages or engines.
wizard.pull-title: Download the local translation model on demand, then start
wizard.video-path-hint: Use Browse to pick a file, or paste an absolute path.
wizard.video-path-hint-browser: Running in the browser: paste an absolute path the orchestrator can read (the native file picker is desktop-only).
wizard.source-language-warn: Make sure this is the language actually spoken in the video. If it is wrong, the transcription will invent text that sounds fluent, and the dub will be confidently wrong with no error shown.
wizard.pull-failed: Could not download the model "{{ model }}".

cloud-phase.refine: review & refine (sends the transcript and the translations)

wizard.output-folder-fallback: The folder you used last time ({{ dir }}) can't be used right now (is that drive connected?), so this project is saved in VideoDubber's default folder, and so are new projects until you choose a folder again.
wizard.output-folder-remember: New projects start in the folder you chose last.
wizard.browse-title: Choose a video file on this computer
wizard.browse-title-browser: The file picker is only in the desktop app. Paste the video's full path instead.
wizard.output-folder-remember-reset: “Use the default folder” here makes them start in the default folder again.
wizard.pack-install-failed: The install did not finish. Press Install to try again.
wizard.preset-hint: A preset fills in the languages, engines, voice and subtitle choices below. Save this form as one to dub a channel's next videos the same way, or many downloads at once (Download screen).
wizard.preset-folder: It also keeps where finished videos are saved: {{folder}}
wizard.preset-folder-named: {{token}} in the folder becomes each project's name, so every series gets a folder of its own.
wizard.preset-series: With this preset, a video longer than {{over}} min is dubbed as a series of {{min}}–{{max}} min parts. Its choices are filled in under "Split into parts": turn that on for a long video.
wizard.preset-series-kept: Saving keeps this series of parts in the preset, even with "Split into parts" off for this video.
wizard.preset-delete-body: Projects already made with it are not changed.
wizard.use-site-subtitles: Use the subtitles the site published, when the downloaded video has them
wizard.use-site-subtitles-hint: Bilibili gives its subtitles (the uploader's, or its own AI ones) only to a signed-in account, so they come with a download once your Bilibili login is set: Download screen, Source account, or Mother Claude passing your browser's cookies. Using them instead of speech-to-text saves the longest step on a long video. The timing is the site's; a video without them is transcribed as usual.

continue-why.video: Choose a video above to continue.
continue-why.languages: Choose the language spoken in the video and the language to dub it into.
continue-why.voice: Wait until the voice has finished downloading.
continue-why.series-ai: Choose the AI that plans the parts (Split into parts), or install the built-in Gemma chat model in Settings → Engines.

leave.creating-title: Leave while the project is being created?
leave.creating-body: VideoDubber is copying the video into the new project. If you leave, the copy carries on and the project appears in Projects when it is done; a notice tells you how it went.
leave.pulling-title: Leave while the translation model downloads?
leave.pulling-body: The download carries on in Ollama, but the dub will not start by itself: when the download is done, open the project in Projects and start it there.

fix.heading: The dub can't start yet:
fix.cloud-key: {{ name }} needs an API key. Add it in Settings, or go back and pick an engine that runs on this computer.
fix.install: {{ name }} needs “{{ pack }}”, which is not installed yet. Install it here: the download carries on if you leave this screen.
fix.ollama-off: Ollama is not running on this computer. Start it, or go back and pick Argos or TranslateGemma for translation: neither needs Ollama.
fix.ollama-model: Ollama is running, but the model “{{ model }}” is not downloaded yet.
fix.downloading: The model {{ name }} needs is still downloading. Try again once it is done.
fix.starting: {{ name }} is still starting. Wait a few seconds, then try again.
fix.model-choice: {{ name }} cannot use the speech model set for new projects. Go back and pick faster-whisper, or choose another speech model in Settings → Speech-to-text.
fix.voice: The chosen voice does not belong to {{ name }}. Go back and choose the voice again.
fix.add-key-hint: This project is kept: come back with “New project” to start it.

builtin.local: Everything runs on this computer: no cloud AI is used, and nothing is sent anywhere.
builtin.kept-local: Your Settings choose {{name}} for {{phase}}; built-in presets stay on this computer. Choose it in the form to use it.
builtin.quality-stt: The largest speech model (large-v3): the fewest recognition mistakes, the slowest, and a download of about 3 GB the first time.
builtin.quality-stt-kept: The largest speech model (large-v3), as recommended for this computer.
builtin.quality-stt-special: The speech model made for this language ({{model}}) is kept.
builtin.quality-review: The Gemma chat model on this computer re-reads the whole translation for names, forms of address and consistency: better lines, slower.
builtin.quality-review-missing: Re-reading the translation needs the Gemma chat model (Settings → Engines): until it is installed, the translation is not re-read.
builtin.quality-fit: Lines too long for their time are rewritten shorter on this computer before anything is sped up.
builtin.quality-speakers: Speakers are detected: each character keeps a voice, and the translation uses the right forms of address.
builtin.quality-speakers-missing: Detecting speakers needs its engine (Settings → Engines): until it is installed, everyone speaks with one voice.
builtin.quality-render: Rendered at the highest picture quality: slower to render, bigger files.
builtin.balanced: What New project picks for this computer: the best engines installed here, with their usual passes.
builtin.economy-stt: A faster speech model (large-v3-turbo) instead of large-v3: several times faster, a little less accurate.
builtin.economy-text: The translation is not re-read and long lines are not rewritten: lines that do not fit are sped up instead (up to {{ratio}}×).
builtin.economy-speakers: No speaker detection: every line is spoken with the project voice.
builtin.economy-render: A fast render: quicker, with a slightly lower picture quality.

wizard.hold-flagged: Stop before voicing while lines still fail the translation checks
wizard.hold-flagged-hint: The app checks every translated line (Chinese letters or a pinyin name in a Vietnamese line, no tone marks, "he/she" alternatives, an untranslated line) and repairs what fails twice with the review model or Gemma. With this on, lines that still fail stop the dub before any voice is made, so you fix them first; continuing voices the lines as they are then. Off: they are voiced and listed in a warning.
wizard.use-burned-in: Use the subtitles burned into the picture as the transcript
wizard.use-burned-in-hint: For a video whose own subtitles are drawn into the picture (most Chinese dramas): the app reads them as text on this computer and makes each one a line, timed by when it shows, instead of transcribing the speech. Names and wording are the video's own. Reads Chinese and English subtitles, in a few minutes per hour of video. If they cannot be read, the speech is transcribed as usual and a warning says why.

subtitle-hint.none: Audio dub only, no caption file.
subtitle-hint.srt-file: A separate translated.srt next to the video.
subtitle-hint.vtt-file: A separate translated.vtt (web) next to the video.
subtitle-hint.embedded-soft: Soft subtitle track muxed into the container.
subtitle-hint.burned-in: Rendered permanently into the video pixels.

original-audio.keep: Keep in background (ducked under the dub)

subtitle-position.auto: Automatic — just above the video's own subtitles when it has them
subtitle-position.raised: Raised — above the video's own subtitles

svc.openai-hint: sk-…  — used by cloud STT, translation and TTS

whisper.base: Base — balanced; good on 8 GB (~145 MB)
whisper.large-v3-turbo: Large v3 Turbo — recommended: near-best, 6-8x faster (~1.6 GB)
whisper.distil-large-v3_5: Distil Large v3.5 — English only, fastest large (~760 MB)
whisper.large-v3: Large v3 — best accuracy, slow on CPU (~3 GB)
whisper.phowhisper-medium: PhoWhisper Medium — best for Vietnamese-source audio

confirm.remove-argos-body: Remove the {{ from }} → {{ to }} Argos pack? You can re-install it anytime.
confirm.remove-engine-body: Remove “{{ name }}” and its downloaded files? You can re-install it anytime.
confirm.remove-key-body: Remove the saved {{ service }} API key? Cloud features for this provider stop working until you add a key again.
confirm.clear-storage-body: This removes {{ packs }} engine pack(s) and all downloaded models and caches{{ size }}. Your projects are kept. VideoDubber re-downloads what it needs on demand.
confirm.discard-edits-body: You have changes that have not been saved. If you leave this screen now they are lost.
confirm.discard-drafts-body: Not saved yet: {{ what }}. If you leave this screen now, these changes are lost.
confirm.clear-downloads-body: Every finished, failed or cancelled download leaves the Download screen and its video file is deleted. Downloads still in progress stay. Projects made from them keep their own copy.

misc.engine-stream-lost: Lost connection to the engine install stream.
misc.engine-stream-lost-fix: The connection to the background service dropped. Try the install again; if it keeps failing, quit and reopen VideoDubber (in a dev build, restart the local services).
misc.heavy-for-machine: May be heavy for this machine — may run slowly
misc.needs-nvidia-driver: Needs NVIDIA driver {{ required }} or newer — this machine has {{ found }}. Update the driver, or use the Vulkan build instead.
misc.needs-ram: Needs about {{ gb }} GB RAM — may run slowly on this machine

ducking-hint.strong: Strong (−18 dB) — background well behind the voice
ducking-hint.very-strong: Very strong (−24 dB) — background barely audible

speed-hint.1-3: Gentle speed-up; expect more timing warnings on dense dialogue.
speed-hint.1-6: Good fit for most content; speech stays clearly intelligible.
speed-hint.1-8: Noticeably brisk speech; few timing warnings.
speed-hint.2-0: Minimizes conflicts; speech can sound rushed.

reason.ram-constrained: With {{ ram }} GB RAM, only the smallest local speech-recognition model fits comfortably; cloud STT will be noticeably more accurate.
reason.ram-balanced: {{ ram }} GB RAM runs “large-v3-turbo” — near-best accuracy at 6-8x the speed of large-v3, a great offline balance.
reason.ram-performance: {{ ram }} GB RAM easily runs “large-v3-turbo”; “large-v3” also fits for maximum accuracy if you accept the extra time.
reason.apple-metal: On Apple Silicon, the llama.cpp (Apple Metal) engine pack runs translation on the GPU. Speech-to-text and voices run on the CPU for now.
reason.slow-cpu: {{ cores }} CPU cores will make local transcription slow on long videos — consider cloud STT for anything over a few minutes.
reason.nvidia: {{ name }} ({{ vram }} GB) detected — install the CUDA engine packs in Settings → Engines for GPU-accelerated transcription and translation. They need NVIDIA driver 551.61 or newer; on an older driver the app falls back to the Vulkan build automatically.

capacity.one-at-a-time: With {{ cores }} CPU cores and {{ ram }} GB of RAM, one dub at a time keeps this computer responsive — a second would mostly make both slower.
capacity.multiple: {{ cores }} CPU cores and {{ ram }} GB of RAM comfortably cover {{ n }} dubs at once (each one wants about 3 cores and a few GB at its peak).
capacity.cpu-bound: The CPU core count is the limiting factor on this machine.
capacity.ram-bound: Installed memory is the limiting factor on this machine.
capacity.hard-cap: Capped at {{ cap }}: past that, the shared transcription/translation/speech services process work one request at a time anyway.
capacity.heavy-engines: Projects that use a downloadable engine (whisper.cpp, TranslateGemma/Gemma, LibreTranslate, vocal separation, forced alignment) always run one at a time, on any computer — those engines take over the machine and stop each other when they overlap.
capacity.manual: Set manually to {{ n }} simultaneous dub(s) (this computer's recommendation is {{ recommended }}).

help.title: Help & diagnostics
help.subtitle: Check that VideoDubber is set up correctly on this machine, and collect everything needed for a bug report.
help.selfcheck-hint: Runs the same checks as the first-run wizard: the built-in services, ffmpeg, disk space and network access.
help.selfcheck-unavailable: The self-check could not run, which usually means the background service is not running yet. Try again in a moment.
help.summary-ok-hint: VideoDubber has everything it needs on this computer.
help.summary-warn-one: It works, with 1 thing to look at
help.summary-warn-many: It works, with {{ n }} things to look at
help.summary-todo-hint: What to do is written under each one.
help.services-hint: The parts that do the work. If one is down, dubbing stops at the step that needs it.
help.services-unavailable: Service status is unavailable — the background service did not answer.
help.report-hint: Copy the diagnostics below into your report. It describes this machine and what went wrong; it is never sent anywhere on its own.
help.privacy: Your home folder is replaced with ~ and any API keys are removed before copying. Nothing leaves this machine until you paste it somewhere yourself.
help.copy-manual: Copying to the clipboard was blocked. Select this text and copy it manually:
help.claude-body: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Mother Claude can run VideoDubber for you: dub a video, follow its progress and fix lines, in your own words. The guide shows how to connect them.

fix.tools: VideoDubber's video tools are missing. Reinstall VideoDubber.
fix.service: This part of VideoDubber is not running. Quit and reopen the app; if it still does not run, export a support bundle below and send it with your report.
fix.network: VideoDubber works offline. Only downloading models, voices and videos needs the internet: connect when you need one.
fix.disk: Free a few GB before downloading bigger models. Settings → Storage shows what takes room and can clear it.

claude-guide.title: Use VideoDubber from Claude
claude-guide.subtitle: Ask Claude to dub a video, check on a project or fix its translation, in your own words. Here is how to set it up, with no terminal needed.
claude-guide.choose-heading: 1. Choose where you talk to Claude
claude-guide.desktop-body: The Claude app for Windows and macOS. One click below connects it.
claude-guide.code-body: Claude in a terminal or an editor. One click below connects it, and Mother Claude sessions use this connection.
claude-guide.mother-body: A desktop app that starts and drives Claude Code sessions, from its window or from a paired phone. Connect Claude Code below and every new Mother Claude session has VideoDubber's tools.
claude-guide.steps-heading: 2. With Mother Claude, step by step
claude-guide.mother-running: Mother Claude {{ version }} is running on this computer.
claude-guide.mother-not-running: Mother Claude isn't running on this computer, or isn't installed yet.
claude-guide.step-install: Install Mother Claude and open it.
claude-guide.step-connect: Connect Claude Code above. You only do this once.
claude-guide.step-session: In Mother Claude, click New session, pick any folder and start it.
claude-guide.step-ask: Ask Claude for what you want done, for example one of the requests below.
claude-guide.step-approve: Approve the cards: each time Claude uses a VideoDubber tool, Mother Claude shows a card asking you, on the desktop and on a paired phone.
claude-guide.approve-allow-for: "Allow for…" on a card remembers that one tool for the session, the project folder or the whole computer.
claude-guide.approve-all-before: To allow every VideoDubber tool at once, add Claude Code's allow rule
claude-guide.approve-all-after: . That is your choice to make: it also lets engine downloads start without asking.
claude-guide.note-new-sessions: Only sessions started after connecting have VideoDubber's tools. Restart a session that was already open.
claude-guide.note-phone: From a phone, Mother Claude can start a new session only in a folder Claude Code has already worked in.
claude-guide.note-accounts: Several Claude accounts: an account that shares the default Claude Code folder sees this connection; an account with its own folder (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) needs its own.
claude-guide.ask-dub: Dub C:\…\video.mp4 from Chinese into Vietnamese
claude-guide.ask-fix: Show me the lines that need attention and fix them
claude-guide.prompts-intro: Two ready-made prompts are slash commands in Claude Code and Mother Claude:
claude-guide.prompt-dub: dub a video with the best quality
claude-guide.prompt-improve: review and improve a dub's translation
claude-guide.prompts-desktop: In Claude Desktop, the same two prompts are in the + menu.
claude-guide.trouble-tools-fix: The session started before you connected: start a new one. In a terminal, this shows the connection:
claude-guide.trouble-not-running-fix: Claude opens the installed app itself and waits up to two minutes for it. If it still doesn't answer, open VideoDubber, wait for the home screen, and ask again.
claude-guide.trouble-other-copy-fix: Claude Code starts a different copy of VideoDubber (after a reinstall or a move). Click Reconnect in the Claude Code row above.

claude-guide.trouble-approvals-fix: A tool call is probably waiting for your approval: check Mother Claude, on the desktop or on your phone.

rec.heading: Recommended for this computer
rec.intro: Optional engines that would make dubbing faster or better on this computer's hardware. Nothing is downloaded unless you choose it.
rec.all-installed: Everything recommended for this computer is installed.
rec.later: You can install or remove these at any time in Settings → Engines. An install keeps running while you use the app; closing the app stops it, and Install picks it up again.

why.whisper-metal: Your Mac's Apple Silicon chip can transcribe speech with Metal, far faster than the CPU build.
why.whisper-gpu: Your {{ gpu }} can transcribe speech much faster than the CPU.
why.whisper-model: The speech model whisper.cpp needs to transcribe: Whisper {{ model }} (~{{ size }} GB), the size recommended for this computer.
why.llm-runtime: Runs TranslateGemma on this computer: a big step up in translation quality over the offline Argos default.
why.tg-cpu: The 4B TranslateGemma (~{{ size }} GB): much better than Argos, and light enough to run without a GPU.
why.tg-4b-gpu: The 4B TranslateGemma (~{{ size }} GB) runs about {{ pct }}% on your GPU. A larger model would spill into system memory and translate at CPU speed, so this is the faster choice here; the 12B and 27B stay installable if you prefer the quality.
why.tg-gpu: The {{ model }} TranslateGemma (~{{ size }} GB) fits your GPU (about {{ pct }}% on the card): the best quality this computer can run at GPU speed.
why.chat-review: A review model (~{{ size }} GB) that re-reads the whole translation for names, pronouns and forms of address. On a real Chinese dub it took acceptable lines from about 4 in 20 to 15 in 20.
why.vieneu-gpu: Natural Vietnamese voices generated on your {{ gpu }}: about 4× faster than on the CPU (a 21-minute video took 2½ minutes on an RTX 3050), with the same voices.
why.vieneu-cpu: Far more natural Vietnamese voices than the built-in Piper voice, generated on the CPU.
why.vieneu38-gpu: The newest VieNeu voices (25 natural Vietnamese voices and voice cloning), generated on your {{ gpu }} many lines at a time.
why.vieneu38-cpu: 25 natural Vietnamese voices across the three regions, and voice cloning from a short recording, on the CPU.
why.separator: Keeps the original music and sound effects under the dub instead of turning everything down.
why.whisperx: Word-accurate timing, and a separate voice for each speaker in videos with several people talking.

voices.title: Voices
voices.subtitle: Listen to, install and favourite voices from every speech engine. Samples play before anything is installed; installed voices work offline.
voices.from-new-project: You are looking at voices for the project you are creating. Everything you entered there is kept: listen here, then go back to choose the voice.
voices.engines-help: Each voice is spoken by an engine. Piper is built in; the others download once, with the first voice you install from them, and then every voice of that engine is ready. With an NVIDIA card you can pick the GPU build for speed.
voices.archived-help: Its maker has stopped updating this model. It keeps working as it is, without fixes.
voices.may-be-slow-help: This computer may run this build slower than recommended (little RAM, or no suitable graphics card). You can still install and use it.
voices.install-engine-body: This voice is spoken by {{ engine }}, which is not on this computer yet. {{ pack }} (about {{ size }}) downloads once; then all {{ voices }} {{ engine }} voices are ready, offline too.
voices.no-preview: No sample yet. Install the voice to hear it.
voices.preview-failed: The sample could not be loaded
voices.speakers-help: This model has several speakers; pick one when you assign the voice in a project.
voices.own-sentence-placeholder: Type a sentence, or leave empty for the sample
voices.own-sentence-help: Installed voices read this sentence when you press ▶ (write it in the voice's language). Voices that are not installed play their sample.

engine-about.vieneu: 25 natural Vietnamese voices across the three regions, and voice cloning from a 3–8 second recording. Runs on the CPU, or an NVIDIA GPU.
engine-about.vieneu-classic: The app's first ten VieNeu voices (such as Ngọc Lan). Kept so older projects sound the same.
engine-about.zerotts: 8 Vietnamese voices (young, middle-aged and older; storytelling, news, commentary). Runs on the CPU.
engine-about.piper: Built in: 183 voices for over 50 languages, each downloaded on its own (20–120 MB). Fast, runs on any computer.
engine-about.kokoro: 54 voices in English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian and Portuguese. No Vietnamese. Runs on the CPU.
engine-about.supertonic: 10 voices, each speaking 31 languages (including Vietnamese, Korean and Japanese; no Chinese). Runs on the CPU. Clear in English and Korean; it reads Vietnamese slowly (lines come out about twice as long), so for Vietnamese VieNeu or ZeroTTS fit the timing better.
engine-about.voxcpm: Cross-lingual voice cloning: keeps the original speaker's voice in a Vietnamese dub. Needs an NVIDIA GPU or an Apple chip.
engine-about.openai: OpenAI's cloud voices, multilingual. Needs an API key in Settings → Cloud services; the text is sent to OpenAI.

license-explain.permissive: CC0, MIT, Apache-2.0…: free to use, commercial use included.
license-explain.attribution: CC BY, CC BY-SA…: usable, commercially too, with credit to the source (hover the badge for the credit line).
license-explain.use-restricted: OpenRAIL: usable, commercially too, except for the uses it forbids; speech must be disclosed as machine-generated.
license-explain.non-commercial: CC BY-NC and research-only data: not for commercial use.
license-explain.service-terms: A cloud service's voices, under that provider's terms.
license-explain.unknown: The source does not state a licence clearly. Hover the badge to see where it comes from, and check before commercial use.

pack-accel.metal: Runs on the Apple chip's GPU

voices.my-help: Record or import a few seconds of speech to make a new dubbing voice (with VieNeu-TTS 3.8). Everything stays on this computer.
voices.my-no-recording-help: This voice works only with the engine it was made with.
voices.my-delete-body: Its recording, voice data and your statement are deleted from this computer. Projects using it will need another voice.
voices.my-export-recording: Include the original recording? It lets the voice be made again for another engine on the other computer, but it is your actual voice: share it only with people you trust.
voices.my-export-folder: Where to save the voice file
voices.my-gender-unconfirmed-help: Choosing voices for the speakers of a video by gender uses this. Pick it once: it is never guessed from how high the voice is.
voices.my-gender-suggest-help: Compares this voice with the built-in voices whose gender is known. It is only a suggestion: you confirm it.
voices.my-gender-no-suggestion: No suggestion: the voice is too close to call, or there is no built-in voice to compare it with. Choose its gender yourself.
voices.my-main-only-help: Casting gives this voice to one main character at most: never to the minor speakers who share voices, and never as the voice of every speaker who has none of their own. For your own voice, say.

voice-clone.title: Make a cloned voice
voice-clone.discard-body: Your recording has not been made into a voice yet. If you close now, it is lost.
voice-clone.engine-needed: Cloning uses the VieNeu-TTS 3.8 engine, which is not installed on this computer yet.
voice-clone.engine-size: {{ pack }} (about {{ size }} GB) downloads once; its 25 preset voices come with it.
voice-clone.engine-background: This window moves on by itself when the install is done. You can also close it: the install keeps going, and the top bar shows how far it is.
voice-clone.engine-unavailable: VieNeu-TTS 3.8 has no build for this computer.
voice-clone.rights-intro: A cloned voice can say anything in the voice of the person recorded. Only clone a voice you have the right to use.
voice-clone.relation-authorized: Someone else's, and they agreed to have it cloned
voice-clone.agree: I have read and agree to the statement above
voice-clone.rights-honest: This is your commitment; the app does not verify identities. It is stored with the voice (word for word, with the time) and deleted when you delete the voice.
voice-clone.record-help: Speak naturally for about 10–15 seconds somewhere quiet, a hand's width from the microphone. The app picks the best part (up to 8 seconds).
voice-clone.script-label: Something to read (or say anything you like, in Vietnamese if you can):
voice-clone.script: Xin chào, đây là giọng nói của tôi. Hôm nay trời đẹp, tôi sẽ kể bạn nghe một câu chuyện ngắn về chuyến đi của mình. Chúng tôi đã đi qua những cánh đồng lúa chín vàng, ghé thăm ngôi chùa cổ và ăn một bát phở thật ngon.
voice-clone.mic-denied: The app is not allowed to use the microphone. Windows: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone → allow desktop apps. macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → turn on VideoDubber, then reopen the app.
voice-clone.mic-none: No microphone found. Connect a microphone or a headset and try again.
voice-clone.mic-busy: Another app is using the microphone (a call, a recorder). Close it and try again.
voice-clone.mic-unsupported: Recording is not available here. Use Import a file with a recording from your phone.
voice-clone.mic-failed: The microphone could not be opened. Try again, or use Import a file.
voice-clone.import-help: Choose an audio or video file with clear speech (a phone memo, MP3, M4A, WAV…). The app reads up to the first 10 minutes and finds the best speech.
voice-clone.check-help: The green part is what the voice is made from; blue marks speech. Move it to choose another part, listen, and read the findings below.
voice-clone.detector-energy-help: The speech-to-text service is not running, so speech was found by loudness; it may be less exact.
voice-clone.voices-isolated-help: Music & voice separation removed the music and sound effects from this audio first, so the voice is copied from the speech alone. Voices copied this way come out cleaner when the video has music under the dialogue.
voice-clone.denoise-help: Turn this off for a studio-clean recording: cleaning can soften the voice slightly.
voice-clone.name: Voice name
voice-clone.keep-recording-help: Needed to remake the voice for another engine later. If off, only the voice data is kept.
voice-clone.local-only: The recording, the voice data and your statement stay on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere.
voice-clone.creating-help: The first time can take a few minutes while the engine loads its model.
voice-clone.done-help: Pick this voice in the project wizard or the editor (voice engine: VieNeu-TTS 3.8). When you publish, say that the voice is AI-generated.
voice-clone.video-intro-track: The app copies the voice of the person speaking in this project's video. It picks the clearest few seconds; you can choose others in the next step.
voice-clone.video-intro-lines: The app copies the voice from the {{ n }} selected line(s) of this video. Choose lines spoken by one person only: lines from several speakers make a mixed voice.
voice-clone.video-intro-speaker: The app copies the voice of Speaker {{ n }} from their clearest lines in this video (lines where nobody else talks).
voice-clone.video-stays: This voice belongs to this project only: it is not added to your voice library, cannot be exported, and is deleted together with the project.
voice-clone.video-analyzing-help: Reading the video's audio and finding the speech. A long video takes a little longer.
voice-clone.video-done-help: Pick it for any line in the editor, or as the whole project's voice in the Project tab (voice engine: VieNeu-TTS 3.8). When you publish, say that the voice is AI-generated.
voice-clone.import-voice-help: Choose a .vdvoice file exported from VideoDubber. It becomes a new voice in My voices, under the declaration you just made.
voice-clone.import-not-voice: This file is not a VideoDubber voice file.
voice-clone.gender-help: Used to give this voice to the men or the women of a video when its speakers are cast. You can change it later in My voices.

speaker-voices.title: A voice for every speaker
speaker-voices.intro: The app copies each chosen speaker's voice from their clearest lines and gives it to them. You can still change any speaker's voice afterwards.
speaker-voices.making-help: About {{ s }} seconds: the app reads the video and makes each voice in turn.
speaker-voices.made: {{ n }} voice(s) made and given to their speakers.
speaker-voices.too-short: only {{ s }} s of clear speech (3 s needed): keeps the project voice. If some of their lines are clear, pick those lines by hand.
speaker-voices.next: Lines whose voice changed are marked for re-voicing: use “Voice N changed lines” in the toolbar.
speaker-voices.next-before-dub: Each speaker will speak with their voice when the dub is made.
speaker-voices.stay: These voices belong to this project only: they are not added to your voice library, cannot be exported, and are deleted together with the project.
speaker-voices.engine-needed: Copying voices needs VieNeu-TTS 3.8. Install it in Voices (a one-time download).

voice-check.speech: {{ s }} s of speech in the chosen part.
voice-check.all-good: A good recording: long enough, clear, not distorted.
voice-check.too-short: Too little speech (at least 3 seconds needed).

fix.too-short: Choose a longer part, or record again and speak for 10 seconds.
fix.short: 6–8 seconds of speech gives a closer voice.
fix.too-quiet: Move closer to the microphone or raise its volume.
fix.clipped: Record again a little further from the microphone, or lower its volume.
fix.noisy: Record somewhere quieter; noise cleaning is on.
fix.long-pause: Move the window to where the speech is continuous.

branding.heading: Logo & greeting
branding.intro: A logo drawn over the video and a short spoken greeting ("Welcome to my channel…"). Both optional; nothing about the dub itself changes.
branding.show-interval: A few seconds every few minutes
branding.logo-hint: Drawing a logo means the video is encoded again, which adds a few minutes per hour of video (less with a graphics card). With subtitles burned in, it adds almost nothing.
branding.logo-bottom-warning: Subtitles sit at the bottom: a logo in a bottom corner can cover them.
branding.at-start: In the first quiet moment of the opening (first {{sec}} s)
branding.greeting-hint: It only plays where nobody speaks (music is fine: it is turned down under the greeting), never before the video. If you ask for more times than fit, it plays as many as fit.
branding.manage: Manage logos and greetings in Settings
branding.kit-empty-logo: No logo yet: add one in Settings → Logo & greeting.
branding.kit-empty-greeting: No greeting yet: add one in Settings → Logo & greeting.
branding.pick-greeting: Choose a greeting sound or video
branding.logo-file-hint: A PNG with a transparent background looks best. JPG and WebP work too.
branding.spoken: Or have a voice say it
branding.spoken-ph: Chào mừng các bạn đến với kênh…
branding.greeting-file-hint: Silence at the start and end is cut and the level is matched to the dub. At most 15 seconds; 2–8 seconds is ideal.
branding.delete-body: Projects that already use it keep their own copy.
branding.placements-hint: Change the times, remove one, or add one at the playhead. Render again mixes it in.
branding.placements-none: It does not play anywhere yet (the next render places it).
branding.placements-preview: This is where the next render will place it.
branding.placement-saved: Saved. Render again to hear it.
branding.opening-skipped: No quiet moment in the opening, so it does not play at the start.
branding.found-fewer: Only {{found}} of {{requested}} times fitted between lines.

series.subtitle: A long video dubbed as a series of shorter parts.
series.analysing: The whole video is being transcribed once. The parts are planned as soon as that is done.
series.not-started: The dub has not started yet (or is paused). Start it to transcribe the whole video once; the parts are planned as soon as that is done.
series.planning: The AI is choosing where to cut and naming the parts…
series.plan-failed: The parts could not be planned.
series.settings-line: Parts of {{min}}–{{max}} minutes, cuts chosen by {{ai}}, each part repeating the last {{recap}} s of the one before.
series.review-hint: Check the cuts and titles: change a start time (m:ss) or a title, then make the parts. A cut always falls in a pause between lines.
series.make-start: Make the parts and start dubbing
series.processing-parent: This run transcribes the whole video once; the dubbing happens in the parts. The series screen shows the plan when it is ready.
series.wizard-intro: A long video (an hour or more) can be dubbed as a series of shorter videos: the first part is ready much sooner, one failure does not hold up the rest, and each part is easier to post. The next part repeats the last few seconds of the one before.
series.wizard-no-ai: This needs an AI set up in Settings: Claude (an API key, or your Claude plan through Mother Claude), OpenAI, Gemini, or the built-in Gemma chat model.
series.wizard-enable: Dub this video as a series of parts
series.wizard-how: The whole video is transcribed once, then the AI picks the cuts among the pauses between lines and names each part. You can check the cuts before the parts are made (unless they start right away).
series.auto-start: Make and dub the parts right away, without stopping to check the cuts
series.stopped-heading: Stopped here for you to check: it was set to start the parts by itself, but
series.all-parts-hint: Pausing or continuing the series acts on every part, in order: nothing done is lost, and they continue in the same order.
series.start-queued: Part {{n}}: waiting its turn in the queue.
series.start-waiting: Part {{n}}: starts once the models it needs have downloaded.
series.start-done: Part {{n}}: already finished, left as it is.
series.start-held: Part {{n}}: you paused it on its own, so it stays paused. Open it and continue it there when you want it dubbed.
series.held-title: This part was paused or stopped by itself, so “Start every part” leaves it as it is. Continue it from its own page.
series.apply-settings: Apply the series settings to every part
series.apply-settings-hint: Copies the series' engines, voices (voices per speaker too), subtitles and mix to each part. A part being dubbed is skipped: pause it first. To hear a change in a finished part, re-dub it from the step the change affects.
series.rebuild: Rebuild parts from the series transcript
series.rebuild-force: Also parts already translated (their translation is discarded)
series.rebuild-hint: After the series transcript was fixed (speakers detected again, loops repaired), each part gets its share of it again, with the series' character sheet. Parts already translated are kept unless you tick the box; a part waiting in the queue is rebuilt where it waits and keeps its turn; a part being dubbed is never touched.
series.report-kept-translated: Part {{n}}: already translated, kept (tick the box to rebuild it too).
series.report-kept-running: Part {{n}}: being dubbed, not touched (pause it first).
series.reason-speakers-failed: speaker detection failed, so every part would be dubbed in one voice. Detect speakers again (editor of the series), then make and start the parts.
series.reason-loops-left: the transcript still has repeated lines flagged as transcription loops. Check them in the editor, then make and start the parts.
series.name-template-hint: {{series}} is the series' name, {{n}} the part's number, {{nn}} the number with two digits (01, 02…), {{total}} how many parts there are, {{title}} the part's title. Leave it empty for the usual names (“<name> - Phần 01”). Finished files saved to a folder you chose are named the same way.
series.name-template-no-number: Add {{n}} or {{nn}}: without the number every part would get the same name.
series.name-template-unknown: {{placeholder}} is not one of the placeholders: use {{series}}, {{n}}, {{nn}}, {{total}} or {{title}}.
series.continues-hint: For a later season of a series already dubbed: the parts keep its name and part names and are numbered from part {{next}}. Once this video's speakers are detected, those who sound like a speaker of “{{name}}” get that speaker's voice; the others get the voices for minor speakers.
series.continues-settings-hint: The same engines, voice engine, subtitles and mix as that series. Its speakers' voices can only be used with the same voice engine.
series.continues-settings-applied: The settings of “{{name}}” are applied. You can still change any of them.
series.continues-total: Total parts on the title cards (optional)
series.continues-total-hint: Empty: as many as there are once this video is split.
series.continues-line: Continues “{{name}}”: its parts are numbered from {{first}}.
series.edit-name: Name (also of its finished files in a folder you chose)
series.edit-hint: Nothing already dubbed is redone. The title is drawn when the video is rendered, so a finished part with a new title is rendered again (only that step).
series.edit-render-again: Part {{n}} shows its new title once it is rendered again: “Start every part” renders it (only that step).
series.rebuild-parts-invalid: Write part numbers such as 23, 24 or 23-30.
series.report-rebuilt-queued: Part {{n}}: rebuilt where it waits in the queue (it keeps its turn), {{old}} → {{lines}} lines, {{speakers}} speaker(s).
series.report-rebuilt-forced: Part {{n}}: rebuilt, {{old}} → {{lines}} lines, {{speakers}} speaker(s); its translation was set aside, so it continues from the translation.
series.replan-keep: Keep the titles and summaries I wrote
series.replan-hint: The AI chooses the cuts and names the parts again. With the box ticked, the titles you wrote stay on the parts that cover the same stretch of the video.
series.reason-transcript-mismatch: the transcript does not match the audio in places, or the audio is completely silent for minutes (a bad join or download). Check those times (Processing lists them), re-transcribe them in the editor, then make and start the parts.
series.per-file-hint: Each joined file becomes one part, cut exactly where it begins, whatever its length. Without it, the parts follow the length above and the AI places the cuts (near the files' ends where it can).

warning.gpu-fallback-busy: The graphics card was busy with another job, so a step ran on the slower CPU build ({{pack}}).
warning.gpu-fallback-failed: A GPU engine ({{pack}}) could not start, so a step ran on the slower CPU build. If it keeps happening, reinstall it in Settings → Engines.
warning.audio-drift: The audio was {{seconds}} s longer than the picture: it was re-timed to the picture, so the dub stays in sync and the video keeps its length.
warning.stt-no-speech: Speech-to-text chunk {{chunk}} of {{chunks}} heard no speech at {{from}}–{{to}}, yet wrote {{count}} line(s) there: they were decoded again, and removed where nothing is said.
warning.stt-no-speech-whole: Speech-to-text wrote {{count}} line(s) at {{from}}–{{to}}, where nobody speaks: they were decoded again, and removed where nothing is said.
warning.digital-silence: {{minutes}} min of complete silence at {{from}}–{{to}} in a video full of talk: probably a problem in the source or its encoding (a bad join or a broken download). Check that part of the video.
warning.transcript-mismatch: The transcript does not match the audio around {{at}}: decoded again, that minute agrees with only {{percent}}% of the lines. Listen to it, and re-transcribe it in the editor if it is wrong.
warning.transcript-mismatch-span: The transcript does not match the audio from {{from}} to {{to}} ({{failed}} spot checks failed): probably a broken source there (a bad join or download). Check that part, and re-transcribe it in the editor.
warning.more-ranges: …and {{count}} more like it (every one of them is in the log).
warning.no-speech-lines: {{count}} line(s) have no words to say ({{examples}}): they stay silent in the dub and keep their subtitle.
warning.songs-suggested: {{count}} line(s) look like a song ({{ranges}}). Nothing was changed: review them in the editor (Project → Songs) and keep the original song where it is one.
warning.speakers-failed: Speaker detection failed ({{cause}}), so the dub uses one voice. Re-detect speakers in the editor.
warning.speakers-unassigned: {{count}} line(s) have no speaker ({{ranges}}), so they would be dubbed in the project voice. Set who says them in the editor, or detect speakers again (Project tab → Speakers).
warning.speakers-low-confidence: {{count}} line(s) were given the nearest speaker, not a sure one. Check them in the editor's Issues.
warning.loops-repaired: {{count}} transcription loop(s) or credit line(s) were repaired: decoded again, or removed where nothing was said.
warning.loops-left: {{count}} range(s) that look like transcription loops could not be repaired: their lines are marked in the editor (Problems). Check them before dubbing.
warning.stt-no-speech-checked: {{count}} line(s) ({{minutes}} min) were written where the speech map heard no speech. A second decode without context checked them: {{kept}} heard again and kept, {{added}} heard only by it and added, {{removed}} removed. Biggest stretches: {{biggest}}. Each change is in the History and can be undone.
warning.lines-flagged: {{count}} line(s) still fail the translation checks after two repairs and are voiced as they are ({{ids}}). Fix them in the editor (Problems) and make their voices again.
warning.lines-flagged-held: {{count}} line(s) still fail the translation checks after two repairs ({{ids}}): the dub stopped before voicing so you can fix them.
warning.timing-conflicts: {{count}} line(s) cannot fit their time even at the fastest speed allowed ({{speed}}×), so they run over into what follows ({{ids}}). Shorten them in the editor, or allow a faster speed.
warning.subtitles-without-lines: {{count}} subtitle(s) of the video itself ({{seconds}} s) have no line under them: speech that was probably lost. Biggest stretches: {{biggest}}. Transcribe those stretches again in the editor, or write the lines.
warning.lines-without-subtitles: {{count}} line(s) have no subtitle of the video under them, while its subtitles follow the dialogue elsewhere: they may be made up. First ones at {{examples}}. Check them in the editor.
warning.burned-in-not-installed: The video's own subtitles could not be its transcript: the subtitle reader is not installed (Settings → Engines & models → Reading burned-in subtitles). Speech-to-text transcribed it instead.
warning.burned-in-no-band: The video's own subtitles could not be its transcript: no band of subtitles was found in the picture. Speech-to-text transcribed it instead.
warning.burned-in-few: The video's own subtitles could not be its transcript: only {{count}} subtitle(s) showed in the picture. Speech-to-text transcribed it instead.
warning.burned-in-failed: The video's own subtitles could not be its transcript: reading them failed ({{reason}}). Speech-to-text transcribed it instead.
warning.burned-in-unreadable: The video's own subtitles could not be its transcript: only {{count}} of the {{total}} subtitles could be read. Speech-to-text transcribed it instead.

diagnostics.heading: Diagnostics
diagnostics.intro: What the app is doing and what went wrong: its own health, the graphics card, the queue, the engines and their last output, disk use, recent warnings and errors, and crash reports.
diagnostics.bundle-hint: A zip of the logs, crash reports and the state above, to attach to a bug report. It never contains API keys or site logins, and your home folder is written as ~.
diagnostics.recovered-plain: It restarted by itself after a stop at {{time}}.
diagnostics.recovered-at: after the background service stopped at {{time}} (code {{code}}).

source-checks.spot-check-hint: Decodes one minute of every half hour again and compares it with the transcript, to find stretches where the transcript does not match the audio (a bad join or a broken download). Adds about 3–5% to speech-to-text. On by default for videos over 2 hours; works for Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
source-checks.drift-longer: The audio was {{seconds}} s longer than the picture: re-timed to the picture
source-checks.drift-match: In step with the picture ({{seconds}} s)
source-checks.drift-shorter: The audio ends {{seconds}} s before the picture: silence fills the rest
source-checks.drift-hint: Measured from the audio's own samples when the audio is extracted. The extracted audio always follows the picture's clock and ends with it, so the dub stays in sync and the video keeps its length.
source-checks.subtitle-check: Check against the video's own subtitles
source-checks.subtitle-check-hint: When the video has subtitles burned into the picture, the app reads where they sit (five times a second, no text recognition) to know when someone speaks. Lines under a subtitle are never removed as silence, and a warning lists subtitles with no line under them (speech that was lost) and lines with no subtitle (maybe made up). Adds a few minutes per hour of video. On by default for Chinese, Japanese and Korean video.
