songs.heading: Songs
songs.intro: A line kept as the original song gets no dub voice: the original audio plays there as it is (the singer too, when the voices are separated), and its subtitle shows only if you turn it on below. Mark lines one by one: dialogue between the lyrics stays dubbed. Mark the selected lines in the Line tab, or keep the ones the app suggests.
songs.count: {{ n }} line(s) kept as the original song
songs.subtitles-hint: Off by default: the original song plays untouched, with no subtitles over it. On: the song lines get subtitles (their translation when there is one). Takes effect at the next render.
songs.subtitles-saved: Saved: the next render uses it.
songs.series-hint: This part’s lines came from its series: the song suggestions are reviewed in the series’ own editor, and lines marked there are marked in this part too.
songs.series-parent-hint: This is a series: lines marked here are marked in every part too (a part being dubbed is skipped).
songs.suggestions-hint: Found after speech-to-text; nothing was changed. Listen to each one, then keep the original song or say it is not one.
songs.keep-all: Keep all {{ n }} as the original song
songs.none: No line looks sung. You can mark songs yourself in the Line tab.
songs.revoice: Done. {{ n }} line(s) shared a voice clip with a song line and need a new voice: use “Voice N changed lines” in the toolbar, then render.
songs.kept: Kept {{ n }} line(s) as the original song.
songs.dismissed: Marked {{ n }} line(s) as not a song: they stay dubbed.
songs.chip-title: Kept as the original song: no dub voice, the original plays here. Its subtitle shows only with “Subtitles for songs” (Project tab).
songs.keep-title: A sung line keeps the original song: no dub voice, the original plays as it is. Dialogue between the lyrics stays dubbed: mark lines, not a whole scene.
songs.keep-selected: Keep {{ n }} as the original song

reason.traditional-title: Written in traditional characters while the rest of the transcript is simplified, next to lines that sound sung: on-screen song lyrics often are. Traditional characters alone do not count: speech-to-text sometimes writes plain dialogue that way.
reason.repeats-title: The same words come back unchanged when the audio is transcribed again: a chorus, not a transcription loop.
reason.sung-title: Very slow, with long held syllables, several lines in a row: singing, not speech.

picture.auto: Find the watermark and blur it by itself
picture.auto-mode: How to hide what it finds
picture.auto-hint: When the video is rendered, VideoDubber looks for a mark that stays still in a corner (about a hundred frames, no AI) and hides it if it stands out clearly (50 % sure or more). What it finds becomes a box here: move it, change it or remove it. Removing the boxes turns this off.
picture.auto-hint-series: The series looks once in the whole video while it is analysed, and every part is made with the box (you see it at review). If nothing stands out, each part looks for its own when it is rendered. Removing the boxes turns this off.
picture.heading: Picture: watermark and the video's own subtitles
picture.intro: Hides a watermark (a channel's name or logo in a corner) and the subtitles the video already has burned in. VideoDubber finds both itself by looking at about a hundred frames: no AI, nothing leaves this computer. They are hidden when the video is rendered, under your subtitles, logo and titles.
picture.detect-hint: Looks for a mark that stays still in a corner, and for the rows where text comes and goes as people speak. Takes 10 to 60 seconds; you can keep working meanwhile.
picture.found-none: Nothing stood out: no still mark in the corners and no subtitles burned into the video. You can still add a box yourself.
picture.found-band: The video's own subtitles found at {{from}}–{{to}} % of the height.
picture.band-guessed: The video has no transcript yet, so its subtitles were found from the picture alone: check the yellow band.
picture.found-no-band: No subtitles burned into the video were found. If it has some, choose a way to hide them below and place the band yourself.
picture.found-check: Check them on the picture, drag or resize them if needed, then save.
picture.frame-alt: A frame of the video with the boxes to hide and the subtitle band drawn on it
picture.frame-loading: Taking a frame of the video…
picture.frame-failed: No frame of the video could be shown: {{why}}
picture.frame-hint: Drag a box to move it, its corner to resize it. The yellow band moves the same way; drag its top or bottom edge to change its height. With the keyboard: arrows move, Alt+arrows resize, Delete removes a box.
picture.no-video: Choose a video first: these options are set by looking at it.
picture.link-video: A video from a link can be looked at once it is downloaded: set these in the editor afterwards.
picture.boxes-hint: Each box is hidden in every frame, or only during the time shown next to it.
picture.box-aria: Box {{n}}: drag to move, drag its corner to resize
picture.confidence-hint: How clearly the mark stood out over the frames. Below 50 %, check that it really is a watermark.
picture.modes-hint: Blur softens the box; Pixelate turns it into coarse blocks; Remove fills it in from the picture around it, which works best for small marks.
picture.add-box-hint: A new box appears in the middle of the picture: drag it onto what should be hidden.
picture.band-aria: Band over the video's own subtitles, {{from}}–{{to}} % of the height: drag to move, drag its edges to resize
picture.band-off: No, leave them as they are
picture.band-solid: Cover them with a solid band
picture.band-hint: The blurred band keeps the picture visible through it and works with every subtitle option. The solid band is drawn together with subtitles burned into the picture, so it only appears with those.
picture.band-solid-needs-burn: Your subtitles are not burned into the picture, so a solid band would not be drawn. Choose the blurred band, or burn the subtitles in.
picture.band-bottom: the bottom strip of the picture
picture.band-strength-hint: 1 blurs lightly, 10 the most. 5 hides most subtitles.
picture.in-band: Put my subtitles inside the band
picture.in-band-hint: Your burned-in subtitles appear where the video's own were, instead of at the bottom. A two-line subtitle grows upward, as the original did.
picture.in-band-needs-burn: Only for subtitles burned into the picture.
picture.apply-parts: Apply to every part of the series
picture.apply-parts-hint: Every part gets the same boxes and band. Times count from the start of the whole video, so each part takes its own stretch. A part being dubbed right now is skipped.
picture.saved: Saved. It takes effect the next time the video is rendered.
picture.running-lock: This project is being dubbed or waits in the queue: you can look, and save once it is paused or done.
picture.render-again-hint: Renders only the picture again, in a few minutes: the voices and the sound mix are kept.
picture.render-parts-confirm: {{n}} parts will be rendered again with the new picture settings, one after another, a few minutes each. Their voices and sound mix are kept.
picture.render-parts-queued: {{n}} parts are waiting to be rendered again.
